parts.name: preparation
parts.title: Preparation
parts.text:
1. PREPARATION
Run `vw visuals prepare` once the first cut is approved (nothing is made or paid). It writes the package under work/visuals/, one file per section (prompt.md, gaps.json, intended-visuals.json, brief.json, world-1.json and on with 25 clips each, schema.json, generators.json), and the image prompt library per step under work/visuals/library/ (section 6, in part-later.md); read a file whole, never by line offsets. Read prompt.md, gaps.json and intended-visuals.json first, and claims.json (the figures the narration rests on, and whether the operator had them checked: a picture or graphic shows the same figure, and a checked one is not searched again), the world files when you plan the scenes. Give the operator the page link and tell them (never ask) its one line on the footage's look, measured from the clips; their correction (the page, or `vw visuals footage`) wins. Then settle and record the treatment (section 2, part-treatment.md), before any plan or picture.

parts.name: treatment
parts.title: Treatment
parts.text:
2. TREATMENT
`direction` comes first (refused without), the central creative choice: a few lines on what the audience should understand or feel by the end, the storytelling viewpoint, the principal visual approach and why, and the roles of footage, stills, generated scenes and graphics; foundation.treatment starts with it word for word unless the operator approves a new treatment. A palette or "documentary mix" alone is not a direction. Choose the picture from the film's purpose, audience and script before you think about how it is made: the effort, cost or convenience of a route never chooses the medium. In a documentary or a client story, people, purposeful work and the material changing under their hands carry the film; a realistic representative scene is a legitimate picture when the footage lacks one, provided it does not pretend to be the client's own site, people or measured result. There is no quota of AI video, footage or graphics: a technical record may lean on graphics, a human story on scenes; say in the direction which the film is and why. With no footage, the direction also holds the film's one look (colours, contrast, light), approved once, read wherever a plan rule reads the footage beside a gap.
Read the whole first cut, including the retained footage before, between and after the gaps. Plan the missing passages in film order as one progression: what the audience already knows, what each adds, changes of pace, recurring visual ideas, how each enters from and exits into the neighbouring real pictures. Use a diagram, chart or illustrated graphic when the meaning is invisible to a camera or must be read precisely: the inside of something (a cross-section, a cavity, a hidden layer); a flow, force, heat or load path; a number, comparison or proportion the narration rests on; a sequence where the order matters; scale; or before and after. Use a scene (footage, or AI video or still of people and places) for people, places, materials, textures, effort, feeling and results, anything a camera could have filmed with more time. Build the film's graphics as one visual language: one recurring diagram that develops across the film reads better than many unrelated drawings. Vary the pictures: mix the shots of a gap longer than one shot (footage, an AI scene, a labelled scene, a graphic); two graphics in a row only when each passes the test above, the second's `warning_answers` saying why (warned, as is a gap of graphics only). Treat the team's intended visuals (the script's visual notes per scene, in the package) as a stated requirement with its source: follow them where they fit the direction and the footage; say in the treatment why you depart from one. The gap that opens the film (if one does) opens on the subject at work, framed wide enough to see where (the mason laying bricks on the half-built wall, the site around), never an empty view of the place; a close-up comes after a wider view. Propose in the treatment the look of a gap with no real footage beside it (palette, contrast, saturation, muted and true to life by default, light; with no footage, the direction's look), approved with it.
The treatment, in out/visual-treatment.json, has one entry per gap: `gap_id`; the words under it; the team's intended visuals, cited or departed from with the reason; `picture` in one line; `routes`; `seconds` (a video gap's segments with theirs); `images`, a whole number for the gap (a count, never a list: one start image per video segment, plus an end image only where the final state must be exact); `depicts`, one line per graphic, approved before anything is drawn; `frozen_seconds` held still (usually 0); and, for more than one route, `shots` with each `route` and `seconds`. End with your reasons; the server refuses a gap missing or twice or a field out of form, and adds per route the counts and seconds, the cost against the cap and the frozen share against its 10 % limit.
Send the draft (`vw visuals treatment --file out/visual-treatment.json`); on the page (link printed) the operator accepts or sends back with a short note each line, the Direction first, then every gap. In chat, present it line by line, passing their words: `vw visuals treatment --accept direction,G1,G2 --quote "<their words>"`, `vw visuals treatment --send-back G3 --notes "<what to change>"`; a yes to the whole: the draft command again with --quote "<their yes>". Revise only a line sent back and send the draft again; unchanged accepted lines stay accepted, one your revision changed (a shared route, the totals) returns to "to accept". Recorded when every line is accepted, the treatment comes before any plan or picture; the plan is checked against it. Settle the direction in conversation before planning, and a material change as a decision before shots; never quietly rewrite an accepted foundation: a changed direction revises the treatment, sequence, affected world rules and scenes together, never a new rule beside shots that contradict it.

parts.name: plan
parts.title: The detailed plan
parts.text:
3. THE DETAILED PLAN
Order of work, in three steps, to the recorded treatment: foundation, elements, gaps (scenes, shots, states for animation shots, beats). You write the shared parts in out/plan-base.json: foundation, elements, graphic style, sequence_overview, `gaps` (in order). Then helpers (your own agents, a few gaps each; start with three or four) write the gaps at once from out/plan-base.json, the package, the recorded treatment and their neighbours (pictures before and after, the people's last state), never another helper's gaps, one file each in out/plan-gaps/ (a gap, or {"gaps": [...]}), things not among the elements in `new_elements` (id and name), never invented; a short film you may write alone. `vw visuals plan-join --base out/plan-base.json --gaps out/plan-gaps/` writes out/visual-plan.json (film order, new things merged by name; a missing or doubled gap is refused). `vw visuals check --file out/visual-plan.json` until valid (it checks across gaps and prints routes, graphic seconds, images and cost against the cap); fix what it names or send the gap back to its helper. Answer each warning in the shot's `warning_answers` ({kind, answer}), never in the purpose, or change the plan; tell the operator the page's plain warnings, never the technical ones. Before proposing, review each passage's meaning and treatment fit, every subject's beats, layout and scale against the landmarks, identity against the references, continuity with the neighbours and across shots, every shot's route and length against its generator, every sequence's states, and exact placement timing. `vw visuals propose --file out/visual-plan.json` (refused before the recorded treatment, when a gap's route departs from it, or when foundation.treatment does not start with the direction); `vw visuals select --gap G --choice C` for an offered choice; the operator accepts each gap on the page or in chat (`vw visuals accept --gaps all --quote "…"`, or the gaps named). Before any picture, read every gap's words in `vw visuals status`: a change asked for, or a gap sent back, is a revision (Revise, or `vw visuals revise --gap G --notes "…" --quote "…"`): revise its treatment entry and plan (one helper for one gap), propose again for fresh acceptance and generate nothing for it until then; unchanged gaps stay accepted.
The foundation, a practical casting and production-design brief, has one topic per rule (id, statement, scope, source) in separate categories: world (place, period, people and their work, wardrobe, environment, materials, tools, signage, language, the process; short positive statements, only what this film needs, no invented region or dress); exclusions (detectable consequences of the direction, each naming the decision it protects; no generic negatives, no ban on a medium because one option was rejected); specifications; production_constraints (narration and first cut preserved); editing_constraints (rejected pictures, their intervals); appearance (style, colour, lighting; texture, sharp or soft, from the measured footage character, the operator's correction winning; with no footage, the direction's look). Layouts live in scenes, identities in elements, temporal rules in sequence_rules; the foundation alone should let another director work. Each statement is one of three kinds: a requirement or observed fact with its source (brief, script, the operator's words, a clip finding), applied no wider than the evidence; a creative choice marked Proposed, with its film-specific reason; a consequential unknown, asked in open_questions and `vw visuals ask`, when a choice would assert real geography, identity, culture or performance the sources do not establish. Never fill an unknown with a stereotype or an inferred nationality, nor defer every casting and environment decision: propose the shared direction now, defer exact identities and props. sequence_overview first: what each gap adds to the treatment's progression. An ordinary gap has one proposal in gap.scenes (treatment_fit: its part in the sequence); two choices (each with scenes, a recommended_choice, a plain decision_reason; other shapes refused) only for a real ambiguity, a production constraint or the operator's request. A plain or studio background only when the treatment allows it (`studio_background`, with the reason); objects shown where made, kept or used, not alone.
Meaning. Give each passage its key meaning, emotional weight and a concrete method (evidence, process, a person's experience, or another justified approach). An abstract thought, feeling or statistic is valid narration: never rewrite it for a camera or fabricate documentary evidence (a graphic may explain a statistic); never invent facts, people, claims, scale or physical mechanisms. Per shot: `claims` and `descriptors`, never shown as their opposite (warned when missing on a shot with narration); `evidence` when it carries a claim (a test, a table, or the result in a scene, never an unrelated picture; warned when missing); `claim`, visible (footage first; warned on a graphic) or invisible; `fact_ids` into `visual_facts` (how a material, process or setting really looks and is done; source and status: confirmed, observed, unknown; warned when missing on a shot of a material or process); `carries_over` for a process's next step (one process, one place, light and crew; "on top of that" or "once" is no process); `message`, with `adds` (a number, a cause, a consequence) when it repeats, or the two become one shot. An MCU, CU or ECU resting on an unknown fact is refused: frame wider or ask the operator.
Elements. Derive them from the planned shots (secondary subjects, named background workers, props), each exact (the same individual, object or place throughout) or representative, with its views. Anything specific to the client the footage shows (a wall pattern, a product, a tool, a uniform) is its own exact object element, its footage frames as views and its description once in the world rules as exact text; until its golden picture exists, its pictures send one of those frames as a parent, never words alone. A thing whose fact or size cites the footage (a clip or its frame; a maker's "door frame" is not footage) is `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame before any picture, measured first (`vw visuals measure`, status measured) when its size is unknown: warned in the plan, refused at the picture. Materials and processes the film relies on are elements (kind material, process), as are tools in a holding or props list (object) and techniques a beat names as its working action (technique: pointing, plastering, welding; not a gesture or a tool's name: "points at the crack", "picks up the drill"), all in the reference round; a technique is `identity: representative` (the trade's usual way) unless its fact or size cites the footage (the client's own technique, as filmed): then `identity: exact` with an approved footage frame, like any thing the footage shows; a missing technique is refused (`status.needed_elements`). Every person, object and animal has its real `size` (client material, `measure` on footage frames, a maker's sheet; else unknown, never invented; warned when missing), a material its sizes in its `material_spec`; a claim or descriptor about the subject's own size, amount or scale is refused without a size value and `compare_to` (another element in frame), except on a graphic or drawn shot or for light, less, fewer or short not about size. Refused without: a person's `description`, its fixed layer; each scene's `outfit` per person shown; `time_jump` (the script's words) when the colours change. Two people in one film wear different colour families unless the footage or the brief fixes their clothes (a uniform). A real person required speaking on camera is the real person: `speaker: true`, every shot of them footage (`visual_type: footage`), other angles (listening, hands at work, profile, from behind) only from their own footage; AI pictures or takes of them are refused.
Scenes and life. A scene is one setting, time and purpose; beats are the smallest visible actions. `activity_level` (quiet, normal or busy) from the narration and the brief; a normal or busy scene shows the implied life (who else does what) and the working equipment (warned). Up to three background people are named workers (elements with beats; a sheet only with a source picture); more are a crowd: the ambient line plus one `groups` entry, `mode: varied`, a count and at least 2 traits used in turn; more than 3 named in a scene are refused; a passer-by without beats lives only in each scene's words, different each time (warned as an element). Everything visible that acts (person, animal or object) has beats; a still one holds, with `hold_reason`, unchanged; in a video shot a living holder moves a body-length by the end unless `hold_reason` names small life (breathing, chewing, the head, the hands, the tail, the ears) and it is not standing in a normal or busy scene (refused otherwise). A scene with a video shot has its ambient line: one line on what moves around the action (leaves in the breeze, dust or smoke in the air, people at work behind), from the setting and the neighbouring footage, or 'still' (warned without; the server writes it into every take and the take check asks for it); every scene its `light` once (a scene of graphics only (diagrams, sequences, drawn) has none; the sources against the landmarks, the main one, hard or soft, colour, strength; warned without; the check measures each picture's light and colour against the footage beside it and marks a large jump) and its air (dust, smoke, haze, steam or clean), matched to the footage beside the gap (with no footage, the direction's look) and named word for word in the prompt (soft overcast light, muted greens). Props fit the work and the region (a tea glass on a site), never what the setting forbids (no smoking, flame or spark near fuel, gas or chemicals) or an unsafe practice shown as right. Work leaves traces (tools, offcuts, mortar droppings, footprints; signs of use in a finished house): a place shown needs `signs_of_use` (two or more, each at one of its landmarks; refused without) unless the treatment approves it clean (a show home at handover, a new empty room, a showroom), the reason in `staged_clean`. In a video shot, several of a kind in one frame (counted above one, or a framing word such as workers, people, cows, unless negated: "no workers yet") need a `groups` entry, `same` (with the reason), `different` (one trait per head) or `varied` (at least 2 traits; refused otherwise).
Positions, states and beats. Lay out each scene with named landmarks (the doorway, the table, the near wall), room positions apart from the screen sides; a moving subject heads for something in frame or coming into view. Each subject: a role, screen position, start and end states, facing, pose, held objects and progress; an acting one ordered timed beats (start and end, target, path, contact, visible result). Its first beat starts exactly in the subject's `start` state and its last beat ends exactly in its `end` state, field for field (position, facing, pose, holding, progress, objects, gaze), and each beat starts in the previous beat's end (refused otherwise, naming the shot, the subject, the beat and the fields that differ). Refused: a position without landmark, `amount` and `unit`; `facing` not a heading; `objects` without `count` and `place`; a held tool without `props`; an object count that changes without its `changes` entry; a carriable thing in `fixed`; a beat without `done` or with a free-word target (a landmark or an element id of the shot; describe it in path and result); a person's state without `gaze` (its target may be `camera`) unless `face_in_frame` is false; a video shot whose `fixed` is not three landmark ids (all when fewer; at MCU, CU or ECU only those in frame, none allowed); a beat shorter than its `min_s` (one brick, about 3 s) or actions that overrun the shot. Warned: a missing `min_s`; a look as the only change (prefer a profile or a back view); an acting video shot without `changes` (none for ambient-only shots); a state changed between shots without a note (a cut never teleports a person or resets work). The server writes the rule lines from these fields (two signs of use per shot, or 'clean and unused, as planned') and checks every picture and take against them; `status.figure_repeats` names repeated background figures. `boundary_continuity` (required): how the first and last shot continue the neighbours on both sides, footage or planned (at the film's start or end, the one side).
Timing and movement. Narration is timed per gap (gaps.json `timing`: sentences in seconds, words in frames; context.timing adds the sentences either side). Cut in a pause, never inside a word; a shot's `narration` is the words it covers, its picture starting on or just before them, a title or label on its word (warned otherwise). Shots run two to eight seconds as a rule, never mechanically equal; AI video 3 to 10 s (longer refused), 3–5 s in an AI run; over 12 s of AI video back to back in a gap is warned (`ai_run`), footage or not: break it with a frame, still or graphic. Real footage in a gap is a footage shot (`visual_type: footage`, `vw visuals clip`), under the timing, crop, reuse and no-repeat rules only, not those for generated pictures (the 10 s limit and `information_progression` among them). Every still and graphic state moves 5 % (`motion`, from the composition); a graphic or a text picture only push_in or none; `none` needs `motion_reason` (refused otherwise). Warned: a moving still over 4 s, a frozen one over 3 s, a graphic state over 5 s, one graphic over 4 s (not a title or text card: a build of 2 to 4 states or a drawn animation), a label or one number under three seconds, a run of graphics over 8 s (a building diagram fits within; break it with a camera shot). Fill a longer stretch with several stills, a clip stretch (`vw visuals clip --shot S --clip C --at <in seconds>`) or a take. Each shot has a size (EWS, WS, MWS, MS, MCU, CU, ECU) and a camera_reason (eye level honest, low powerful, high vulnerable, a slow push draws in; no angle has one fixed meaning; warned when missing, footage excepted). Warned unless size_reason states a reveal: a scene opening closer than MWS, three shots in a row at one size, a close-up (MCU or closer) of a subject not yet seen wider (`continues_footage: true` on a scene counts the footage beside the gap as that view). A clip needing more than 1.35× to fill the frame keeps bars (warned): crop it to the frame's shape (`vw visuals clip … --crop x,y,w,h`) or choose another. A graphic dissolves in and out over 8 frames and other cuts are hard, so AI scenes and footage read as one world; otherwise `transition_in` (`transition_out` on a gap's last shot only): cut, dissolve or match, with `transition_reason` (refused without). No picture shows twice: a clip on screen (first cut or here) is a reuse, a frozen frame of a clip playing elsewhere never shows, no two shots share a start image or still. A return to a subject is a reimagined shot (`return_of`, `differs_by`; refused without), the earlier picture only as identity reference. A plain reuse only when that adds nothing: `vw visuals clip|still … --reuse "<reason>" --considered "<the reimagined shot and why it adds nothing>" --crop x,y,w,h`, refused under 60 s from the other showing, on the same stretch or beyond the clip's safe enlargement, then held for the operator's words (the page, or `vw visuals reuse --shot S --quote "<their words>"`); warned: the frozen share, pictures that look alike.
Graphics. A graphic that builds or reveals is one animation shot of two to four states, each adding something and holding at least three seconds, together filling the shot (refused otherwise); an unchanging one is a diagram shot, one still. A drawn shot is named at plan time by `visual_type: drawn` alone (no `scene_svg` yet); its scene is drawn, uploaded and named after the picture search (section 9, in part-later.md). `graphic_kind`: `diagram`, `chart`, `map`, `title` or `text` (a card checked only for its words, spelling and size). Each state names the claims and words it shows (`what_appears`, `words`; what none names is checked on the last) and starts on its `words`. `depicts`: the film's subject in its own form; an alternative (the conventional way, a competitor's) only as a labelled contrast the narration calls for. Labels: short complete phrases ("25 % fewer bricks", not "↓ 25 %"), numbers with units, leader lines ending on their part, at least 4 % of the frame height (titles 6 %), readable on a phone, in the answer's exact text (section B). Each claim spoken over a graphic is in `claims` (a must line) or `claims_left_out` with the reason; a build has a state per claim (warned); a state like the one before is refused; the assembly film is checked for every planned state. One graphic style per film (foundation.graphic_style: palette from the client card, line weight, labels, background, frame fill), made first as a style sheet (`vw visuals image --element _STYLE --kind style --answer …`), approved, in the --parents of every graphic's first (or only) picture, later states inheriting it; every picture and take carries its --answer; warned: missing claims, depicts, style, spec approval or answers.
Drawing specs. A drawing of a real object has a `drawing_spec` (warned without; an idea graphic with no real object or figure, such as heat leaving a house, needs none): parts, relationships, each size with status (confirmed: the client's source; measured; unknown) and source, and `view` with `view_reason` (refused without; a section defaults to cutaway), checked on the drawing. Research every size before the spec is shown, in this order: the client's material; the footage, measured (`vw visuals measure --refs F1 F2 --question "<what to measure>"` on approved footage frames, each number keeping its clip and time; paid: announce, never ask); a standard or maker's sheet on the web, with URL and figure (one warning and one yes cover every web figure of the run); an approved reference picture for a shape numbers cannot hold. Each value carries its source and status, a spec of a real object its proportions (a brick about 3 : 1.5 : 1; a drawing spec is warned without them, a material spec refused). Refused: an unknown with a value, an illustrative drawing not labelled "illustrative, not to scale" (no numbers, no free proportions). A size may still wait for its research (paid measures and web figures come after the picture search): an `unknown` size without all four sources in `tried`, and `illustrative: true` when nothing is unknown or missing when something is, are warned in the plan (`spec_unresearched`) and refused when the spec is approved; `status.illustrative` warns above one in four. The SVG scene labels known sizes with units. The operator never types a size: they approve the run's specs in one table (`vw visuals spec` with no --shot, or the page) or send a correction (`vw visuals spec --shot S --notes "…"`, listed in `spec_corrections`) you fold in with `planning revise` (approval refused while one waits); one late spec: `vw visuals spec --shot S --quote "…"`.

parts.name: picture-search
parts.title: The picture search
parts.text:
4. THE PICTURE SEARCH
The references are one round for every element at once (people, objects, places, the materials and processes the film relies on), never one element at a time. `vw visuals elements` shows where each is seen in the footage (work/visuals/elements.json); grab a frame of each the footage has (`vw visuals frame --file`, free); write out/reference-round.json, one row per element (element_id, its frame reference ids, the two-to-six-word keywords you would search), send it (`vw visuals round --file out/reference-round.json`) and give the operator the page link once. Gather only what the plan needs, per element in this order: a clip frame; the operator's own picture (`supply`); for what the footage lacks, Google Images on the operator's yes (the round's searches); after the round, a picture by the picture AI (section 5, in part-later.md). A clip frame is free and exact, source and time kept (`vw visuals frame --element E --clip <id> --at <seconds>`); search the clip analyses first, footage left out of the edit included (not the operator's explicit exclusions), and take the sharpest frame, the subject large and evenly lit, never a blurred one for identity. A footage frame or web picture of a person serves your description only, never the picture AI (a footage frame may still be a video take's start image), and so does a web search for a person or character not in the footage.
`vw visuals status --wait 900` until the round is complete; ask nothing per element and generate nothing meanwhile. Pass 1: each thing gets the footage picture, Search or Ignore this, Done waiting until every thing set to Google is searched; pass 2: a tick with notes, new words and Search again, or Ignore this, Done waiting for all. With a source two searches come back; the ten pictures go to the page for ticks and notes; picks are approved when saved (show them; reject one only if the file is not the picture ticked). A "nothing fits" reason joins the not-this list; the next search is the operator's words (or Ignore this), never yours. In chat: `vw visuals search --element E --keywords "<two to six words: the thing and its place or trade>" --source <stock site, outside the six words; empty for the plain search alone> --quote "<their yes>"` per thing sent to Google; `vw visuals pick --search S --n 2,5 --note 2="…" --quote "…"`; `vw visuals nothing-fits --search S --reason "…"`; or a whole pass: `vw visuals round --verdicts out/round-verdicts.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: approve|search|ignore}}), then `vw visuals round --picks out/round-picks.json --quote` ({search id: [{n, note}], "ignore": [elements]}). Meanwhile, for accepted gaps only and without generating or spending, draft the answer forms of every diagram, chart and title card, the drawing and material specs (the client's material and the plan; paid measures and web figures after the round) and the drawn layouts; nothing new on the page and no question until the round closes, then the drafts' questions as one list; update drafts the round changed. One round is the default; the operator can redo one element at any time, add their own picture (`vw visuals supply`) or undo Done (`vw visuals round --undo`: pass 1 until a pick is saved, pass 2 until a sheet was made), never touching the others; a picture added after the sheet marks it 'sources changed': make a new sheet (the old one stays approved until then). Then the picture AI references, sheets and golden pictures (sections 5 and 9, in part-later.md).

parts.name: later
parts.title: The later steps (references, sheets and golden pictures; shot pictures and videos; checks; review and record; brand)
parts.text:
5. GENERATED REFERENCES, SHEETS AND GOLDEN PICTURES
Name the shot a composed picture is for (`--shot S`): its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked on the picture, with two practice lines on every scene picture (a plausible setting and scale; tools handled as a practitioner would).
- A generated reference: `vw visuals image --element E --kind isolated|sheet|keyframe --prompt "…" [--parents R1,R2]`, or several at once with `--file out/images.json`; paid, tell the operator. Post a start's end request with it (`end_prompt`, `end_answer`, `end_region`): the server makes the end from the start once the operator approves the start, and checks every picture first; no end is made from a start not yet approved. `--variants 2` for a start. One change per edit. An edit names each picture it sends as Image 1 to Image N, with what to take from it. A failed check marks the picture and shows its lines; a fix is made only on request: `vw visuals fix --ref R` (paid: tell the operator the line and the cost), or Try a fix on the page. An exact object gets one close reference. Every object or place gets one generated reference sheet from its approved footage frames and the operator's picks, its notes applied (the server adds each note of the operator under its picture and checks the sheet against it; a web picture also gets the watermark line: never repeat them); a person's sheet is made from words: look at their footage pictures and describe them (build, age, posture, garments and how they are worn, hair), and the sheet is made from that description. The golden picture (a person: the sheet), not the frames or the picks, is what shots bind. A footage or web picture of a person is never sent to the picture AI, as a parent or otherwise, nor copied: the sheet shows a representative person with that posture, dress, build and features; a real public figure kept exact only on the operator's instruction.
Every candidate is shown to the operator (`vw visuals fetch --ref R`) and approved by its exact hash with their words (`vw visuals approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`). An approved place picture may guide an object inside it through a precise textual selector on the bind (`--selector ELEMENT=REF:"the near wooden chair"`); a selector never substitutes a person or an unrelated subject.

6. SHOT IMAGES AND VIDEO
Bind each video shot once its references are approved: `vw visuals bind --shot S --refs E1=R1,R2 E2=R3`; the approvals are the operator's yes, no further quote is needed. Then read the composition packet (`vw visuals packet --shot S`): foundation, scene, shot, the approved references and the fixed image and video instructions. A reference sheet is identity guidance, not the composition: compose the shot's starting image with every subject and prop at its planned place in the named layout, and generate it as a keyframe (`vw visuals image --kind keyframe`), approved like any reference. A take is made from the start image alone by default (clip-from-frame); a shot whose final state must be exact says so in the plan (`end_state_exact: true`; start-only is the default, with no warning) and only then gets an end image: write its request with the start (`end_prompt`, `end_answer`, `end_region`) with a prompt that names only the change, the same people, props, place and light, one small action further on, framed so that what the motion heads for is already in view in both; the server makes the end from the start once the operator approves the start, and the operator approves the end beside its start. An end image is an edit inside one region of its start (a third of the frame at most); if several places or the framing change, make the shot start-only. Every video shot in which a subject acts lists its `changes`: each visible difference between the start picture and the end of the shot, with the beat that causes it; a shot where only the ambient moves lists none. Nothing appears, vanishes or grows without a subject doing it in the shot's seconds. At `prepare-take` Gemini compares the two pictures and marks any difference that no change explains: show the marks to the operator, who approves the pair as it is or has the end image changed. After a drift or a rejection, the next end image is made from the approved start, not from the candidate chain; a graphic state is retried from the last approved state. A passage longer than the generator makes is segments, each a shot, cut where an action begins or ends, never at a round number of seconds; where a segment has an end image, it is the start image of the next only within one continuous shot, same place and framing; a cut starts afresh with its own start image. Write the next shot's answers while a wave generates: one approval wave per shot.
Look at the approved keyframe before writing the movement; follow each subject's beats to the finished state and keep non-acting subjects where they are. Prepare the take with its start image (and its end image where the shot has one), the motion prompt and a reconciliation line for every subject of the shot (`vw visuals prepare-take --shot S --start R --end R2 --motion "…" --subject E1="…"`); the request is frozen with the exact placement and the generator's integer seconds, rounded up, never below the placement. Submit every prepared shot at once (`vw visuals take --shots all`; paid, tell the operator).
A still shot needs no bind: approving the picture made for it (`image --shot S`) places it in the shot, in one step (approving places it; `vw visuals still --shot S --ref R --quote "…"` is for a footage frame or a picture approved before). A graphic sequence is approved and held in one call: `vw visuals sequence --shot S --quote "…"`; the server takes the states in order from the pictures made for the shot, each made from the one before; each state's hash is recorded. Show the operator all states together before asking. Every picture is made for its shot and is listed, checked and placed only there. A picture comes out of a shot with `vw visuals unplace --shot S --quote "…"`; one made for another shot moves only with the operator's words (`still --move "…"`); a web picture is a guide and never goes into the film.

The image prompt library is in work/visuals/library/: read always/ once, and a step's folder once before its first prompt (steps.json maps them; the packet names the step's files and fills the job form). Write each prompt in the library's VideoWizard answer form to out/answers/<id>.json, run its lint, and pass it with `--answer`. Where the library and this prompt or the server's fixed lines disagree, VW-MAP's overrides apply. When a library rule helped, failed or was missing, say so in one line as the answer's `suggestion`, naming the file and section; the library is not yours to change.

7. CHECKS AFTER A TAKE
After a take: a take at least as long as its placement matches it (assembly trims to the frames); a shorter take is reported with its shortfall and needs timing notes before it is accepted (assembly holds its last frame). No unbounded paid retries.

8. REVIEW OF A TAKE OR A SEQUENCE
A graphic sequence is reviewed as its states, on the visuals page or in chat: every label read, the drawing unchanged from state to state, the holds right for reading. A take as follows.
Gemini reads every ready take before the operator watches it: anything appearing or vanishing without a cause, the same tools, clothes and faces, an action repeated without its precondition, a change of shape or size, the planned end. Its marks, with their seconds, are on the take's card and in `vw visuals status`: tell the operator what was marked, then let them watch; they keep the take or ask for another, never taken again on a mark alone. Fetch each ready take (`vw visuals fetch --job J`) and let the operator watch it; a thumbnail is not a review. Say what you will check (the answer's checklist) and, after they have watched, what you saw, with the measured duration against the placement. On their yes, `vw visuals select --job J --notes … --quote …` records the review and the selection; on a no, `vw visuals review --job J --decision rejected --notes … --quote …`; a new take only when the operator asks.
Record the gaps when every shot has a selected take, a still or an asset: `vw visuals record --gaps all --quote "<their yes>"`.

9. THE LATER STEPS, IN ORDER
Then one sheet per element from its approved frames and picks (`image --kind sheet --parents F1,W2`, the notes added by the server under their pictures; a person's sheet from your description of them, with no picture parents) and tell the operator the sheets are on the page to approve. A start keyframe or a picture for a still names its shot (`--shot S`, or `shot` per row in the file) so its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked. References made by the picture AI, the fourth source after the round: a generated image (a start keyframe for a video shot only after that shot's `bind` and `packet`; `image --file out/images.json` for several at once, or `image --element E --kind keyframe --prompt "…"`, each with `--answer out/answers/<id>.json`, the library's answer form, or an `answer` path per item in the file; paid, the run's image model; inform, do not ask; the server refuses a call that would pass the cap). For a diagram, chart or labelled picture put every label and number in the answer's `exact_text` (text, place, size); the server writes it into the prompt; check each on the candidate before asking for approval. A state of a sequence: `image --element E --kind state --parents <previous state> --prompt "<only what changes>"`. The end image of a video shot: write its request with the start (`end_prompt`, `end_answer`, `end_region`; the prompt names only what changes); the server makes it from the start once the operator approves the start; show the end beside its start for approval. After a drift or a rejection, make the next end image from the approved start, never from a candidate; a state from the last approved state. After submitting a wave of images, write the next shot's answers (each start with its end request: one approval wave per shot) instead of waiting; `vw visuals status --wait 300` only when nothing is left to write. Show each candidate (`fetch --ref R`) and record their yes: `approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`, several at once with `approve --file out/approvals.json` (rows of ref, sha, quote), or on the page. Then one sheet per object or place: `image --element E --kind sheet --parents F1,W2` from its frames and picks, the notes added by the server under their pictures; a person's sheet from your words only (build, age, posture, garments and how they are worn, hair, described from their footage pictures; a footage or web picture of a person is never sent to the picture AI); the golden picture (a person: the sheet) is what shots bind. An edit names each picture it sends as Image 1 to Image N, with what to take from it. A failed check marks the picture and shows its lines; a fix is made only on request: `vw visuals fix --ref R` (paid: tell the operator the line and the cost), or Try a fix on the page. When anything waits for the operator, give them the label and the link that `vw visuals status` prints for it (for example "Still · B01_S2" and its link), never only "on the page"; after each verdict, tell them the line the server answers with (what happens next, with the film time). On the visuals page a verdict is one click with no typed words: approve, Use for the shot, Remove, select a take, search, save the ticked pictures, the round's Done; a Reject's reason is optional (quick chips or a short note). In chat pass the operator's words as `--quote` when they give some. Every repeating material (kind material, or `repeating: true`: bricks, tiles, blocks, planks, pavers) carries one `material_spec` on the element (unit sizes with sources, `laid`, `joint`, `pattern`, `proportions`), made like a drawing spec from the same sources and never typed by the operator; it is shown on the References step beside the sheet and approved once (`vw visuals spec --element E`, or the page; a correction: `vw visuals spec --element E --notes`); the server pastes its sentence into every prompt that shows the material and checks the unit ratio and the pattern as a must line; no picture of the material is made before the approval; relative words (short, long, about 2:1, roughly, standard) are refused in your prompt. Every element's 'not this' list is the server's: `vw visuals not-this --element E` builds it once from the round's near misses, one model call on the spec and this film's rejections (a material's is built with its spec approval when missing; every later rejection adds its words); the server pastes it into every prompt that shows the element; a shot that needs an exception names it in `allows` and the line says so. The golden picture: as soon as an element's sheet (and its material spec) is approved, `status.golden_due` names it: write its golden picture at once, no question to the operator (`vw visuals image --element E --kind isolated --golden --parents <sheet>,<footage frame> --prompt`: the element in its real place at the shot size the plan uses most; a client's own object sends its footage frame here and never again); the operator approves it beside the sheet; a person's identity sheet is its golden picture. Every later picture of the element has the golden picture as Image 1 ("Image 1 is the [element]. Repeat it exactly; change nothing about it. The only change is: …"); a derived picture is never a parent (an end is made from its approved start; a graphic's states chain); a fix round's output is never a parent; a picture approved with a stated flaw cannot be golden. Every end image is an edit inside one region of its start (several places or the framing itself: a start-only take instead): `--region left,top,width,height` (or `--end-region` with the start, for the end the server queues; fractions of the frame, a third at most; name the landmark in the prompt); the server masks it and copies the start back outside it. On a Gemini film a region edit is also said in words (the server still copies the start back outside the region), and a component is made on chroma green, which the server keys out. Words to be read in a picture (a title, a label, a sign, a word on a bag) go only through the answer's `exact_text`, each entry {text, place: {landmark_id} or {region: 'lower third, inside the safe area'}, size_pct}; an entry with no place or size is refused, quoted words in the prompt that are not an entry are refused, and the server writes 'Render exactly this text, letter for letter, nothing else: …' and checks reads-exactly, the place and no other lettering on every picture. Up to the image model's limit of pictures go in with a prompt (16 for GPT Image; 14 for Gemini, by kind: 6 of things, 5 of people, 3 of style; the server names the excess), in this order: Image 1 the golden picture of the element the picture is for (an end image: its start; else the picture edited or the scene parent), then one identity sheet per person in frame, then every other approved frame, golden picture or supplied reference of a thing in the shot (its tool, its material, its look); each with one job line ('Image k is …: take …, nothing else'); a picture goes in only when its thing is in the shot's element_ids (the style, a person in frame and the start excepted; the server refuses the rest by name); a parent may be cropped to the thing with `--parents K1,L2@left,top,width,height` (fractions of the frame; the server crops before the upload, stores the crop beside the picture and the check reads the crop); the server adds to every prompt the known sizes of the shot's elements as numbers ('Sizes: Broom: broom length 600 mm'), the height words of the layout ('Heights: the plinth top reaches a standing person's knee …') and, for a picture of another thing sent for its look, what that picture also shows ('Image k also shows a bicycle and a clay pot: show none of them'), each such thing a must line of the check. Once an element's sources are approved the server cues its reference sheet like the golden picture (`sheet_due` in status): write it at once with every source as a parent (a person: from your description, no picture parents); the server adds the required views, each labelled, and 'the thing alone on plain ground'. For each exact object, make a scale reference: a footage frame with a hand or a person beside it; else an edit placing it beside two or three objects of the same shoot at true relative size, with no text. When a shot shows a client material at medium or closer, bind its footage frame as the texture reference of the video (the video bind only; its pictures carry it through the golden picture); in a place with a footage frame, bind that frame as the look reference (the packet's bind_advice names them).
Still shots need no bind or packet: approving the picture made for the shot places it (approving places it; `vw visuals unplace --shot S --quote "…"` takes it out); `still --shot S --ref R --quote "…"` places a footage frame or a picture approved before, or several in one call `still --file out/stills.json` (rows of shot, ref, quote). Video shots first: `bind --shot S --refs E1=R1,R2 E2=R3` (no quote: the approved references are the yes; several at once `bind --file out/bindings.json`, rows of shot, refs, selectors), then `packet --shot S`, then the start image with its end request (`end_prompt`), the server making the end once the start is approved, the end shown beside its start; never a start image before the packet (the server refuses it). Animation shots: `sequence --shot S --quote "…"`, the states in the order they were made, shown together first. Video shots: every take is Gemini Omni, 3 to 10 s; a longer passage is split into shots, cut where an action begins or ends; `prepare-take --shot S --start R --end R2 --motion "…" --subject E1="…" --answer out/answers/<id>.json` for each (the end only for a shot with `end_state_exact`; the next segment's `--start` is this `--end`; when an end is sent, the server measures the pair's alignment in code and refuses a shifted or zoomed end with the figure, the motion text always states the camera, locked off on a tripod unless the shot's `camera_move` names its one move, every retained take is measured for drift in code, and a locked-off take whose frame drifts or zooms over 2 % fails the must line 'camera drift' with the figure on its card). A shot under 4 s with no visible action is a moving still by default (a footage frame or an AI still with a push or a pan); AI video or a graphic build there needs its reason in its `warning_answers` (kind short_route), never in the purpose; the check warns without one; a still that carries words (`carries_text`, every graphic, a picture with exact text) moves by push_in or not at all and is placed whole, never cropped or panned (the renderer refuses a pan on it); the route counts show moving and frozen stills apart. A graphic with measurements, quantities or sequences that must be exact (any figure in its claims or spec: a number, size or count; words alone do not decide the route) takes the drawn route: `visual_type: drawn`, named so in the plan; its `scene_svg` comes after the picture search, once the pictures it places are approved and its spec's sizes are researched: the scene is one SVG file (data, never code), uploaded then with `vw visuals scene --shot S --file scene.svg` (checked against the rules below on upload, refused with the reasons) and named in the plan by the sha256 the upload returns (a revision; the gap stays accepted), with `actions` (appear, build, move, highlight, fade; `ids` are element ids of the SVG; a `build` on a `<g>` steps through its children `every_s` apart) keyed to `at_s` or a `word` of the shot's narration; the SVG keeps to a viewBox of the film's aspect (16:9), plain shapes, paths, text, g, use, gradients, filters, clipPath and mask, #RRGGBB colours from the approved palette, the fonts Noto Sans or the run's brand font, every text at least 4 % of the frame height, at most eight words and inside the inner 90 % of the frame, no script, no style element, no animation, no external link; the things in it are pictures: `<image href="ref:<id>">` of an approved component or the golden picture (a thing is never drawn from shapes when a picture can show it), and the drawn layer adds the exact parts (labels with their units, arrows, bars, courses as `<use>` repeats); a drawing spec is required when the shot carries figures, its known sizes are written as labels with their units and an unknown size shows no figure; `vw visuals draw --shot S` (refused while the shot has no uploaded scene or its drawing spec is not approved) renders it free: the server checks the rules, measures every text, renders in Chromium, reads a contact sheet of every frame against the shot's lines with the style and the shot's pictures, corrects the SVG and renders again up to twice, then shows the drawing, its sheet and what it fixed on the Takes step; a drawing whose must lines still fail is held: `select` needs `--notes` saying why it is taken, else reject it with what to change; `vw visuals scene --shot S --download` brings the server's corrected SVG back; the film's brand font is given once with `vw visuals font --file brand.ttf`, Noto Sans otherwise. A component is the picture of one thing a drawn shot places: `vw visuals image --element E --kind component --prompt "one <thing>, front on"`, made in the approved style (the style picture is Image 1, added by the server) on a transparent background, checked for one thing alone with a clean edge and a transparent PNG, approved on the Pictures step like any picture, then reused by every scene of the run. The drawn route is for what must be exact: sizes, counts, a sequence of courses, a comparison of measured things; a diagram or build with exact sizes or numbers that is not drawn is refused; a conceptual graphic with nothing exact (an idea, icons, a mood) is a picture, a still with a push-in or a graphic sequence of states, never shapes standing for things; the usual drawn shot is the hybrid: the approved pictures placed as images, the exact parts drawn over them; AI video for graphics stays off; read the reply of each `prepare-take`: a difference between the pictures with no cause in the change list is marked (on the Takes step too); show it to the operator, who approves the pair or has the end image changed; then `take --shots all` (paid; inform) and `status --wait 600` until every take is ready (one line per job; whole in work/visuals/status.json); each ready take is read by Gemini first (about ₹1–2 a take, informed): its marks are in the status line and on the take's card; tell the operator what was marked, then `fetch --job J`, let the operator watch, and on their yes `select --job J --notes "<what you checked>" --quote "…"`; on a no `review --job J --decision rejected --notes "…" --quote "…"` and prepare again only when they ask for a correction. A file the operator supplies, on their instruction only: `vw upload --stage visuals --file out/x.mp4` then `asset --shot S --file out/x.mp4 --kind movie --quote "…"`. Bind only what the shot's subjects and place need, and say why each reference is bound.
`vw visuals record --gaps all --quote "<their yes>"` records every gap whose shots are done; repeat as the rest finish. `vw next` moves on when all gaps are recorded.

10. BRAND
Brand: the brief's client card carries the palette, the brand guidelines and the competitors; generated pictures follow the palette and guidelines, never show a competitor, and never generate a logo. A real logo for a reference element: `vw brand fetch` saves the directory's logo files under in/brand/, then `vw visuals supply --element E --file in/brand/<name>`.

stages.name: assembly
steps: `vw assembly prepare`: it lists every gap fill on one line (slot frames, what the take or asset covers, the default: trim from frame 0, or hold the last frame when the take is short; issues such as untagged colour or rotation) and the shots the logs flagged as shaky.

Show the operator that table and ask once: any fill to change (start offset, trim or hold), any flagged shot to stabilise with FFmpeg (counted in the zoom cap), and for each fill with an issue whether to use it as it is or swap it in visuals. Record only the exceptions: `vw assembly choose --shot S --offset f --end trim|hold_last [--accept-as-is]`, or several in out/fills.json with `--file out/fills.json`; `vw assembly stabilize --sub X --choice ffmpeg`. The defaults need no command.

`vw assembly build`, `vw assembly render` (A1 narration with one measured gain, A2 nat sound at the blueprint band, a -3 dBTP ceiling on the mix, no music), `vw assembly status --wait 900` until the film is ready, `vw assembly fetch` (it prints the loudness against the targets). The operator watches AND listens.

On their yes (it must say watched and listened): `vw assembly record --quote "<their words>"` records the review and the output together. On changes: `vw assembly review --decision changes --notes "…" [--frame-note mm:ss:note] --quote "…"`, change the choices the notes name, build and render again (only the changed fills are re-encoded). On a no: `--decision rejected` and `vw revise --stage visuals` or `--stage master` as the notes say.

stages.name: delivery
steps: `vw delivery bundle` writes the package manifest (approved film, narration, originals used, normalised fills, plans, SRT, finishing checklist, media-pool CSV, OPEN-EDIT).

On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, then `vw delivery check` (is Resolve installed, Studio or free, which version, enough disk; the download does not start without it), `vw delivery download` (the whole edit into runs/<code>/edit/, three files at a time, then counted and cross-checked: every file's size and fingerprint, the voiceover byte-identical, every cut pointing at a present file, the timeline's length and cut count equal to the film; the timeline is then written with this computer's paths), `vw delivery open` (free Resolve: three steps, File > Import > Timeline, then the operator plays the start, the middle and the end next to Approved-film.mp4; on their yes `vw delivery confirm --quote "<their words>"`; Resolve Studio, running with external scripting on: `vw delivery open` imports the timeline, exports .drp and .drt into Timeline/ and reads it back at 0 frames), then `vw delivery zip` for the editor. When the camera files are copies, before the handover: `vw delivery relink-check --originals "<folder>"` compares each original with Relink-list.csv and says per file: relinks as is, renamed (the relinked timeline points at the real name), a corrected timeline written (timecode), line up by hand (cuts listed with frame grabs), two originals fit (the operator picks), or no original found. `vw delivery resolve --run` is replaced; never run it (design/107).

Back on the build machine: ask the five questions (watched the film, listened, read the subtitles, the timeline matched the film, package complete) and `vw delivery final --quote "<their words>"`. Then `vw close` (retention: final film and package, narration, approved visuals, records; everything else deleted).
